reading.h2: Great Lent: A Journey to the Resurrection

reading.quote: Death is swallowed up in victory… O Death, where is your sting? O Hades, where is your victory?… But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

reading.p: The Great Lent fast is a long season of fasting, prayer, repentance, and self-denial that prepares us for Easter. It is a journey with Christ that disciplines the flesh and trains the soul to turn away from sin and to be made ready for His Passion and Resurrection.

list: Abiy Tsom (Great Lent): prepare, repent, fast, and pray.
Holy Week: walk with Christ through His suffering and Cross.
Fasika: celebrate that Christ rose and conquered death.

reading.p: For the next fifty days after Fasika, we continue celebrating until Pentecost, which is the descent of the Holy Spirit on the Apostles and the public life of the Church. During this season the regular Wednesday and Friday fasting is suspended.
Today we have most of our community gathered here. These are the holidays when most of us come together, just as so many came to celebrate Hosanna.

reading.h2: The Message: The Church Is the Hospital of the Soul

reading.p: My message to everyone is this: the Oriental Orthodox Church is the true original Church, instituted by Christ. It is an Apostolic Church preserved by the Apostles and the Church Fathers, and it is the hospital of our soul. Here we find the Body and Blood of Christ.
We remember the story of Deacon Mirehet and of the early Church Fathers. As St. Athanasius of Alexandria said, "God became man so that man could become god."
Theosis means becoming united with God by His grace and becoming more like Him. This does not mean that we become God by nature or become equal to Him.

reading.quote: He who says he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.
He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.

reading.p: Our Church embodies this. Salvation was given by Christ, and we celebrate it together with God's mercy, love, and compassion. Yet through this, our transformation is required: through His grace we are transformed, share in His divine life by grace, and grow into holiness. This is what our Church provides, a hospital that transforms and heals us through our traditions and Sacraments, such as Baptism, confession, and Holy Communion.

reading.h3: Christ Is the Head, We Are the Body

reading.p: My brothers and sisters, Christ is the Head of the Church, and we are the Body of the Church.

list: He protects and saves the Church.
The Church must remain united to Him.

reading.p: Most of the world is looking for God. Within the Church we find Him; we find His Body and His Blood, the medicine of the soul. In Holy Communion, we partake of His Body and Blood, abide in Him, receive eternal life, and share in the power of His death and Resurrection.

The world is changing. When I was young, nobody understood why I celebrated Christmas in January or Easter later than the rest. They did not understand why my church service started early in the morning or why I could not always eat the school lunch. Today they know; today they witness the power of the Church and of our Lord and Savior who leads it.

As we celebrate the victory of Christ, this victory given to us as Christians, let us acknowledge the Church, the opportunity and gift we have to partake in Communion, and let us continue the legacy of the Church.
We are the future of the Church. This is not simply about a baton being passed down to us from our parents; the baton was first given to us by Christ.

My deacon brothers, remember whom we serve. My mezemurans, remember whom we praise. To all of the youth and young adults here today, remember whom we worship, and remember the Church. Christ has risen.
To the newcomers of the Church, we open our arms to you so that you may learn. We teach theology on Fridays at 6:00 PM, and you are welcome to come.

studyGuide.overview: Great Lent (Abiy Tsom) is a season of fasting, prayer, repentance, and self-denial that, through Holy Week, leads to Fasika, the celebration of Christ's victory over death. The lesson presents the Oriental Orthodox Church as the original, Apostolic Church and the hospital of the soul, where through the Sacraments believers share in Christ's divine life by grace (theosis).
keyPoints: Great Lent is a journey with Christ that disciplines the flesh and prepares the soul for His Passion and Resurrection.
The three phases are Abiy Tsom (fasting and repentance), Holy Week (walking with Christ to the Cross), and Fasika (the Resurrection).
For fifty days after Fasika, celebration continues to Pentecost, and Wednesday and Friday fasting is suspended.
The Church is the hospital of the soul, healing and transforming us through its traditions and Sacraments.
Theosis is becoming united with God and like Him by grace, not by nature; we are transformed and grow into holiness.
Christ is the Head of the Church and we are His Body; in Holy Communion we receive His Body and Blood, the medicine of the soul.
The youth are the future of the Church, and the baton was first given by Christ.
reviewQuestions: What are the three phases of the Great Lent journey, and what does each one mean?
What happens during the fifty days after Fasika, and why is regular fasting suspended?
What does it mean that the Church is the 'hospital of the soul'?
How does the lesson define theosis, and what does it carefully say theosis does NOT mean?
Why is Holy Communion called the 'medicine of the soul'?
What does it mean to say the baton was 'first given to us by Christ'?

checks: The observance of Abiy Tsom culminating in Fasika, Holy Week, and the fifty days to Pentecost reflects the Tewahedo liturgical calendar.
Theosis is stated correctly: union with and likeness to God by grace, explicitly NOT becoming God by nature or equal to Him, guarding against any heretical reading.
The Eucharist is affirmed as the true Body and Blood of Christ and the medicine of the soul, consistent with Orthodox sacramental theology.
The Church is identified as the original Apostolic (Oriental Orthodox / non-Chalcedonian) Church; the saying of St. Athanasius and the Scripture citations are reproduced as given.
No Chalcedonian or Filioque language is present, and nothing contradicts the Miaphysite confession; the Holy Spirit is named in the descent at Pentecost without procession claims.
